title: Geometric Valence Neutrality — Structure Has No Fixed Moral Sign
purpose: Prevent the project from assigning permanent moral/theological meaning to geometric primitives such as high/low, wide/narrow, circle/line, wall/open, cord/free, cube/sphere or center/periphery. Valence must be derived from function, destination, dynamics, relation, consequence and textual context.
principle: No primitive geometric feature is morally positive or negative merely because of its shape, dimension, orientation, enclosure or scale.

biblical_counterexamples.negative_wide: Matthew 7:13-14 uses the broad/wide way for the route leading to destruction.
biblical_counterexamples.positive_wide: Psalm 118:5 describes divine rescue from distress into freedom/a broad or spacious place; Psalm 119:32 links broadened/enlarged heart or understanding with running the commanded way.
biblical_counterexamples.conclusion: Width alone has no stable moral sign.

biblical_counterexamples.negative: Isaiah 5:18 uses cords/rope for dragging iniquity; Psalm 18:4-5 uses cords/ropes of death/Sheol and snares.
biblical_counterexamples.positive: Hosea 11:4 uses cords/bands of kindness/love with feeding and eased burden; Ecclesiastes 4:12 presents a three-strand cord as resistance to being quickly broken.
biblical_counterexamples.conclusion: Cord can mean destructive attachment, mortality, guidance/love or resilience depending on function.

biblical_counterexamples.ordinary_protection: Walls frequently signify defense and city boundary.
biblical_counterexamples.wallless_positive: Zechariah 2:1-5 measures Jerusalem and then describes it as inhabited without walls because of abundance, with God as a wall of fire around and glory within.
biblical_counterexamples.conclusion: Material enclosure is not identical with security; boundary function can be carried by a different protective mechanism.

biblical_counterexamples.positive: Revelation 21:15-17 measures the holy city, its gates and wall; its length, width and height are equal.
biblical_counterexamples.project_correction: A cube-like/foursquare geometry cannot be treated as intrinsically shadow, prison, Saturnian or evil merely from shape.
biblical_counterexamples.conclusion: The same geometric family can participate in a positive eschatological image.

biblical_counterexamples.negative: Psalm 22 hostile surrounding and the project's pathological closed-loop return can be shadow uses.
biblical_counterexamples.positive: Proverbs 8:27 / Job 26:10 use circle/boundary imagery in ordered creation; protective surrounding occurs elsewhere in biblical poetry.
biblical_counterexamples.conclusion: Circle can signify order, protection, totality, recurrence or entrapment.

biblical_counterexamples.negative_high: Pride/exaltation traditions can make height negative.
biblical_counterexamples.positive_low: Valleys can become sites of guidance, restoration or renewed life; Isaiah 40/Luke 3 level both mountains and valleys in preparation of a way.
biblical_counterexamples.project_correction: Peak is not automatically good and valley is not automatically bad.

scientific_corollaries: A scalar coordinate has no ethical sign until an objective/function is declared.
A stable attractor can be healthy or pathological; stability alone does not establish value.
A narrow feasible set can represent safety or oppression; a broad set can represent freedom or uncontrolled danger.
A boundary can preserve function, deny legitimate passage, channel flow or define measurement; topology alone does not supply ethics.
Centrality can represent coordination or capture; graph structure requires functional interpretation.
Symmetry can indicate order or rigidity; asymmetry can indicate specialization or imbalance.
archive_rules: Every moralized geometry claim should name the operative function and outcome.
Do not infer evil from circle, cube, darkness, low position, mud, enclosure or repetition without contextual evidence.
Do not infer holiness from height, light, straightness, centrality, openness or ascent without contextual evidence.
When scripture supplies opposite-valence uses of the same geometry, preserve both as a deliberate anti-flattening control.
Scientific graphs/metrics should use neutral variable names where possible; moral labels belong to a separate interpretation layer.
